lines: My landlord said I should have shared my salmon with his wife. So I followed his lease. Word for word.
I work in food service. I rent the basement, and I share a kitchen with my landlords.
The lease is very clear. I can use the kitchen. But each household keeps its own food separate.
My first night there, I shared some leftover shrimp Alfredo. Just being nice.
Big mistake.
A few days later, I cooked two pieces of salmon and some cilantro-lime rice. For me.
My landlord walked in, opened the oven, and looked inside.
Then he told me I should have shared it with his pregnant wife.
And that maybe he'd have to reconsider my lease.
So I sent him a photo. Of his own lease. The part that says food stays separate.
And I made him an offer.
I'll cook one meal a week for you. You buy the ingredients, and you take $50 off my rent.
They said no.
And they reminded me I couldn't break my sixty-day lease early without paying.
Fine. I started planning my move.
And I kept cooking. For myself.
Garlic short ribs. Hot honey fried chicken.
Then my electricity started acting up.
It stopped the moment I mentioned calling the fire marshal.
Then there was an incident with air freshener, sprayed right next to my roast.
After that, they mostly left me alone.
I moved out, and stayed with a coworker until my new studio was ready.
My own studio. My own kitchen. And nobody opening my oven.
